subject: harlequin beetle
title: Arachnids Ride Under a Beetle's Wings, and Males Fight Over the Seats

scenes.text: This beetle carries hidden passengers under its wings.
They're pseudoscorpions: arachnids a few millimetres long, with pincers but no tail.
A whole crowd rides one harlequin beetle to reach freshly fallen fig trees, where they live.
The biggest males take over the beetle, blocking rival males from boarding but letting females on.
They mate on the way, and a male can keep his beetle for up to two weeks.
So the beetle isn't just flying. It's running a bus.

description:
Pseudoscorpions (Cordylochernes scorpioides) hitch rides under the wing covers of the harlequin beetle to reach newly dead fig trees.
Large males take control of a beetle, keep rival males off and let females board, mating with them during the trip; a male may stay aboard for days or up to two weeks.
What's the strangest way an animal travels?
thumbnail_text: A BEETLE THAT RUNS A BUS
first_comment: Imagine fighting for a seat under someone's wings for two weeks. What should we cover next?
